Keywords: Orthohantavirus, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, Dobrava– Belgrade virus, Puumala virus, Southeastern Europe, zoonoses, One Health approach. 4 INTRODUCTION Human-pathogenic orthohantaviruses (family Hantaviridae) are among the most important rodent-borne zoonotic viruses worldwide and are responsible for the clinical syndromes collectively referred to as hantavirus disease [1,2]. Throughout this review, the term orthohantavirus is used when referring to the virus taxonomy, whereas hantavirus disease and related clinical terminology are retained for consistency with established medical nomenclature. In Eurasia, hantavirus infections primarily manifest as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), whereas in the Americas they cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS, also known as HPS) [3,4]. Their public health significance extends beyond their clinical impact and reflects their remarkable ability to persist silently within particular small-mammal reservoir hosts, amplify under favorable ecological conditions, and periodically emerge as geographically focal outbreaks in human populations [5–7]. Consequently, hantavirus disease represents a paradigmatic example of a zoonotic pathogen shaped by complex interactions among viral biology, reservoir ecology, land use, and climatic conditions [6–8]. In Europe, the epidemiological and public-health landscape is dominated by Old World orthohantaviruses, particularly Puumala virus (PUUV) and Dobrava–Belgrade virus (DOBV), that vary in reservoir associations, ecological niches, geographical distribution, and typical disease severity, yet together account for the majority of the regional HFRS burden [4,9,10]. Southeastern Europe (SEE) occupies a unique position within the European orthohantavirus landscape and cannot be viewed merely as a southern extension of the PUUV-dominated ecosystems of Central and Northern Europe. Rather it represents one of the few European macro-regions where highly pathogenic DOBV lineages and less virulent PUUV strains coexist in shared ecological and clinical space, thereby contributing to a heterogeneous regional risk signature that cannot be understood with respect to northern-European nephropathia epidemica models alone [4,9]. As no single definition of SEE exists, for the purposes of this review the region comprises Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH), Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia. SEE countries have played an important role in hantavirus research, as DOBV was first identified in the former Yugoslavia [10]. The region remains characterized by endemic circulation of orthohantaviruses in both human populations and rodent reservoirs, with marked 5 geographic heterogeneity and localized transmission foci. Thus, human infections and evidence of viral circulation have been documented across all countries included in the study [11–16] . Although clinical reporting remains limited in some parts of the region, there is evidence of ongoing viral circulation throughout. Renewed interest in hantavirus disease across SEE has been driven by climatic variability, changing reservoir ecology, land-use change, and evolving human exposure patterns, all of which contribute to dynamic transmission risk across the region [5,17–19]. Therefore, hantavirus disease in SEE should be interpreted not as a static endemicity problem, but as a dynamic interface between reservoir ecology, environmental change, and human activities. Accordingly, this review synthesizes current evidence on hantavirus epidemiology, clinical characteristics, ecological drivers, and public health challenges across SEE, with particular emphasis on regional outbreak patterns and cross-border epidemiological dynamics. Search strategy and data sources This review was based on a structured search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify literature relevant to orthohantavirus disease in Southeastern Europe. Searches covered publications available from database inception until June 2026 and combined terms including “hantavirus”, “orthohantavirus”, “hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome”, “Southeastern Europe”, “Balkans”, and the names of individual countries within the study region. Additional relevant publications were identified through manual screening of reference lists of eligible articles. The review focuses on the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, transmission dynamics, and public health implications of human hantavirus infections in Southeastern Europe. As this is a narrative review, studies were selected according to their relevance to the scope of the manuscript rather than through formal systematic-review methodology. The epidemiological data presented in Table 2 were compiled from multiple complementary sources, including annual surveillance reports of the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), official national public health reports, and country-specific datasets provided or verified by collaborating public health experts where available. Given the heterogeneity of surveillance systems, reporting practices, and laboratory confirmation procedures across countries, epidemiological 6 data were interpreted descriptively. The primary data source for each country is summarized in Table S1. For countries with ECDC-derived data, EU-level surveillance through TESSy is available from 2008 onward; therefore, our comparative analysis covers 2008–2024, while earlier years are reported as N/A. Heyman et al. independently documented laboratory-diagnosed hantavirus infections in Greece, Slovenia, Romania, and Bulgaria during 2005–2007 [20]. We cite these findings as evidence of earlier hantavirus activity, but do not combine them with the ECDC or national data because the two sources are based on different surveillance approaches. Annual incidence rates were calculated as: Incidence (per 100,000 population) = (annual number of reported HFRS cases / corresponding annual mid-year population estimate) × 100,000. Annual country-specific mid-year population estimates were obtained from the World Bank DataBank, World Development Indicators (indicator SP.POP.TOTL) and matched to the corresponding surveillance year for each country. World Bank data were accessed on July 9 2026 [21]. Epidemiology of hantavirus infections in Southeastern Europe HFRS has been recognized in SEE for more than half a century, and the region remains a well-established endemic region characterized by sporadic cases each year punctuated by periodic epidemics [9]. A distinct north-south gradient is evident across the region, with PUUV being relatively more common in the northern part of the region, and DOBV predominating in the southern Balkans [9,22]. SEE is also the cradle of DOBV taxonomy: the prototype Dobrava strain was recovered from yellow- necked mouse (A. flavicollis) in Slovenia, while Belgrade virus was isolated from a fatal HFRS case in Serbia, with both subsequently confirmed as genetically identical [10,23]. DOBV and PUUV co-circulate widely across the Balkans, with generally moderate reported regional incidence but subject to marked interannual variability driven by multi-annual rodent population cycles [19]. Outbreaks typically follow mast-seeding events and favorable climatic conditions, including winters that enhance rodent survival and reproduction [4,6,7]. 7 Subclinical infections are common, with estimated subclinical-to-clinical ratios ranging from 5:1 to 20:1, resulting in substantial under-ascertainment, particularly of mild PUUV-associated disease [19,24,25]. Seroepidemiological surveys indicate substantial background exposure with a clear geographic gradient: overall seroprevalence has been estimated at approximately 6% in BiH, approximately 4% in Greece (range 0 to 14% by county), 3.1% in Bulgaria, 1.7% in Slovenia, and 1.6% in Croatia, with higher rates reported among occupationally exposed populations and local foci [9,14,25–29]. Evidence of viral circulation has been documented across the SEE region, although the dominant virus and disease burden vary according to local ecology, rodent-host distribution, and surveillance intensity (Table 1). Albania and Kosovo were not included in the comparative surveillance analysis presented in Table 2 because continuous annual surveillance data were not publicly available for inclusion; therefore, the information presented for these countries is based primarily on the available published evidence. BiH has been a major endemic focus of hantavirus infections in Europe for more than 50 years. Outbreaks have been documented since 1967, with large epidemics in the former Yugoslavia during 1986-1987 and 1989, involving more than 1,000 reported cases, and further outbreaks in 1995 and 2002, the latter implicating PUUV, DOBV and untyped serotypes [30–34] . Following the 2002 epidemic, hantavirus infections continued to occur regularly in BiH, with at least one confirmed case reported annually between 2005 and 2024 (Table 2). Although annual case numbers were generally low, pronounced peaks were observed in 2014, 2017, and 2021, supporting the persistence of endemic circulation with periodic outbreaks. While the majority of reported cases originate from central and northeastern Bosnia, the distribution of rodent reservoirs and serological evidence of exposure indicate that hantavirus circulation extends beyond these recognized endemic foci [27,35]. Consequently, the geographic distribution of infection may be broader than that indicated by routine surveillance data. In Croatia, both DOBV and PUUV contribute to disease burden, with a notable military outbreak in 1995, and large epidemics in 2002, 2012, 2014, 2017, and 2021. Notably, the 2012 Medvednica outbreak was linked to exceptionally high PUUV infection rates in bank voles, while the 2017 (≈389 notified cases) and 2021 (≈334 8 cases) outbreaks were the largest on record and extended into Adriatic-coastal and other areas previously considered non-endemic [18,36,37]. Serbia has reported HFRS since 1961, with Belgrade virus characterized during a 1989 epidemic and subsequent molecular confirmation of DOBV circulation foci in western and central regions [10,38,39] . Serbian national surveillance demonstrates persistent endemic HFRS activity, with generally low annual incidence punctuated by occasional increases in reported cases. In Greece, serological evidence dates to 1981, with 0–4 HFRS cases reported annually in recent years and an estimated case-fatality of approximately 9% among hospitalized patients, a figure derived from severely ill cases and therefore an overestimate of the overall rate [14,40]. DOBV (genotype Dobrava, hosted by A. flavicollis) predominates, with 80% of all cases occurring in endemic foci in the Rhodope and Pindos mountains near the northern borders and no cases reported from southern Greece or the islands, whereas PUUV is also endemic but accounts for far fewer recognized cases [10,14] . Despite relatively low annual notification rates, the persistence of endemic foci and serological evidence of exposure indicate continuous viral circulation, emphasizing the importance of maintaining surveillance in northern Greece. Bulgaria has recorded HFRS since the 1950s, mainly across the Rila-Pirin-Rodopi massifs of the southwest, where phylogenetically related DOBV strains circulate in Apodemus mice, confirming local rodent reservoirs [9,10,16]. Although reported incidence has remained consistently low, the continued detection of DOBV in both rodents and human cases supports persistent endemic transmission rather than sporadic viral introduction. Albania likewise has confirmed hantavirus circulation through genetic detection in rodent hosts [12,41–43], while Kosovo reports severe DOBV-associated HFRS, with documented population seroconversion in endemic zones and severe sporadic cases [15,44,45]. Slovenia represents one of the most affected countries in SEE, experiencing recurrent large-scale outbreaks and the highest incidence rates recorded in the region, particularly during 2012, 2019, and 2021. In contrast, Montenegro reports relatively few cases but periodically reaches among the highest annual incidence rates in SEE 9 owing to its small population size, illustrating the importance of interpreting incidence alongside absolute case numbers [46] . North Macedonia has reported only sporadic cases in recent years, although limited surveillance coverage makes it difficult to determine the true extent of endemic circulation [11]. Hantavirus infections in Romania remain rare but endemic, with sporadic cases reported over the past two decades, primarily caused by DOBV [4,13] . Despite the low number of reported cases, increasing recognition through improved diagnostics and surveillance suggests that hantavirus infections may be more widespread than previously appreciated. The comparative analysis of 20-year surveillance data presented in Table 2, based on long-term national surveillance data and complemented by ECDC surveillance reports and published national epidemiological studies, further illustrates the heterogeneous yet interconnected epidemiological landscape of hantavirus infections in SEE. papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 在东南欧的感染 - 流行病学、暴发动态与 One Health 准备:叙述性综述。

analysis_zh.background: 在人类致病的 正汉坦病毒 中,它们是欧洲重要的鼠媒人畜共患病原体,东南欧 (SEE) 独特地同时存在循环的 Dobrava‐Belgrade 病毒 (DOBV) 和 普马拉病毒 (PUUV),导致不同严重程度的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述综合了 汉坦病毒 在 SEE 各地区的流行病学、传播动力学、临床特征、生态驱动因素以及公共卫生挑战,突出显示了持续的地方性传播、地域和年度间的异质性,以及较轻的 PUUV 与较重的 DOBV 疾病共存的情况。
analysis_zh.current_state: 长期监测显示,地方性传播持续存在且存在显著的地域和年度间异质性;斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚负担最重,且活动高峰(2008、2012、2014、2017、2019、2021、2023)部分同步,分别对应鼠类种群波动、阔叶树丰产和气候变异。
analysis_zh.gaps: 本叙述性综述依赖于对国家和欧洲监测数据的描述性评估,而这些数据在能力和完整性上存在差异,导致区域内出现数据缺口和潜在的漏报。
analysis_zh.future_research: 在协调的 One Health 框架下,整合人类、动物、环境和基因组监测对于提升暴发预测、跨境准备以及未来在 SEE 的疾病控制至关重要。

papers.full_text: RAZAFINDRALAMBO Nadia Kaloina ARENAVIRUS ET HANTAVIRUS CHEZ LES PETITS MAMMIFERES SAUVAGES TERRESTRES DE MADAGASCAR IDENTIFIES PAR RT-PCR Thèse de Doctorat en Médecine Vétérinaire UNIVERSITE D’ANTANANARIVO FACULTE DE MEDECINE DEPARTEMENT D’ENSEINGNEMENT DES SCIENCES ET DE MEDECINE VETERINAIRES ANNEE : 2011 N° :064 ARENAVIRUS ET HANTAVIRUS CHEZ LES PETITS MAMMIFERES SAUVAGES TERRESTRES DE MADAGASCAR IDENTIFIES PAR RT-PCR THESE Présentée et soutenue publiquement le 16 septembre 2011 à Antananarivo par Mademoiselle RAZAFINDRALAMBO Nadia Kaloina Née le 30 Septembre 1988 à Soavinandriana Antananarivo Pour obtenir le grade de << DOCTEUR EN MEDECINE VETERINAIRE >> (Diplôme d’Etat) Directeur de thèse : Professeur RASAMINDRAKOTROKA Andry MEMBRES DU JURY Président : Professeur RASAMINDRAKOTROKA Andry Juges : Professeur RANDRIANJAFISAMINDRAKOTROKA Nantenaina Soa Professeur RAKOTOZANDRINDRAINY Raphaël Rapporteur : Dr RASOLOFO RAZANAMPARANY Voahangy DEDICACE Je dédie cette thèse : A DIEU Tout Puissant : qui m’a donné la vie et m’a accordé la chance de faire cette thèse. Qu’Il nous accorde sa grâce. « Je t’instruirai et te montrerai la voie que tu dois suivre ; Je te conseillerai, J’aurai le regard sur toi » Psaumes 328 A mes parents : pour tant d’année de sacrifice vos encouragements, votre soutien moral et matériel et votre optimisme dans la vie, m’ont marqué, des qualités qui ont fait de vous des parents exemplaires. Je n’ai pas le mot pour dire ce que je ressens. Veuillez trouvez dans cet humble ouvrage les récompenses de vos efforts. Que la bénédiction de Dieu vous accompagne durant toute votre vie pour qu’Il vous donne mille fois plus que ce que vous avez donné. A mes amis A tous ceux qui ont contribué de loin ou de près à la réalisation de ce travail. A NOTRE MAITRE DIRECTEUR ET PRESIDENT DE THESE Monsieur le Docteur RASAMINDRAKOTROKA Andry Professeur Titulaire d’Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche en Immunologie à la Faculté de Médecine d’Antananarivo. « Vous avez accepté de diriger cette thèse et vous avez accueilli sans reserve et avec bienveillance malgré vos incompréhensibles obligations. full_text_sections.full_text: RAZAFINDRALAMBO Nadia Kaloina ARENAVIRUS ET HANTAVIRUS CHEZ LES PETITS MAMMIFERES SAUVAGES TERRESTRES DE MADAGASCAR IDENTIFIES PAR RT-PCR Thèse de Doctorat en Médecine Vétérinaire UNIVERSITE D’ANTANANARIVO FACULTE DE MEDECINE DEPARTEMENT D’ENSEINGNEMENT DES SCIENCES ET DE MEDECINE VETERINAIRES ANNEE : 2011 N° :064 ARENAVIRUS ET HANTAVIRUS CHEZ LES PETITS MAMMIFERES SAUVAGES TERRESTRES DE MADAGASCAR IDENTIFIES PAR RT-PCR THESE Présentée et soutenue publiquement le 16 septembre 2011 à Antananarivo par Mademoiselle RAZAFINDRALAMBO Nadia Kaloina Née le 30 Septembre 1988 à Soavinandriana Antananarivo Pour obtenir le grade de << DOCTEUR EN MEDECINE VETERINAIRE >> (Diplôme d’Etat) Directeur de thèse : Professeur RASAMINDRAKOTROKA Andry MEMBRES DU JURY Président : Professeur RASAMINDRAKOTROKA Andry Juges : Professeur RANDRIANJAFISAMINDRAKOTROKA Nantenaina Soa Professeur RAKOTOZANDRINDRAINY Raphaël Rapporteur : Dr RASOLOFO RAZANAMPARANY Voahangy DEDICACE Je dédie cette thèse : A DIEU Tout Puissant : qui m’a donné la vie et m’a accordé la chance de faire cette thèse. Qu’Il nous accorde sa grâce. « Je t’instruirai et te montrerai la voie que tu dois suivre ; Je te conseillerai, J’aurai le regard sur toi » Psaumes 328 A mes parents : pour tant d’année de sacrifice vos encouragements, votre soutien moral et matériel et votre optimisme dans la vie, m’ont marqué, des qualités qui ont fait de vous des parents exemplaires. Je n’ai pas le mot pour dire ce que je ressens. Veuillez trouvez dans cet humble ouvrage les récompenses de vos efforts. Ce travail est le modeste témoignage de toute mon affection et mon profond respect. Qu’il soit le témoin de mon immense reconnaissance. Que Dieu le Tout Puissant vous garde. Amen A mes sœurs : pour leur support et encouragement, recevez ma tendre affection. Que l’esprit de fraternité nous anime pour toujours. A mes oncles et mes tantes paternels et maternels, à toutes les familles : Je n’ai rien à vous offrir en guise de récompenses. Que la bénédiction de Dieu vous accompagne durant toute votre vie pour qu’Il vous donne mille fois plus que ce que vous avez donné. A mes amis A tous ceux qui ont contribué de loin ou de près à la réalisation de ce travail. A NOTRE MAITRE DIRECTEUR ET PRESIDENT DE THESE Monsieur le Docteur RASAMINDRAKOTROKA Andry Professeur Titulaire d’Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche en Immunologie à la Faculté de Médecine d’Antananarivo. « Vous avez accepté de diriger cette thèse et vous avez accueilli sans reserve et avec bienveillance malgré vos incompréhensibles obligations. Vous nous faites aussi l’honneur d’accepter de présider notre thèse. Veuillez trouver à travers ce travail l’expression de notre profonde gratitude » A NOS MAITRES ET HONORABLES JUGES DE THESE Monsieur le Docteur RANDRIANJAFISAMINDRAKOTROKA Nantenaina Soa Professeur Titulaire d’Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche en Anatomie Pathologique à la Faculté de Médecine d’Antananarivo. Monsieur le Docteur RAKOTOZANDRINDRAINY Raphaël Professeur Spécialiste en Microbiologie et Parasitologie à l’Ecole Supérieure des Sciences Agronomiques. Enseignant à la Faculté de Médecine d’Antananarivo et au Département d’Enseignement des Sciences et de Médecine Vétérinaires. Nous vous remercions d’avoir accepté de juger ce travail, un peu éloigné de vos préoccupations habituelles. Veuillez bien trouver ici le témoignage de notre respectueuse reconnaissance. A NOTRE RAPPORTEUR DE THESE : Madame le Docteur RASOLOFO RAZANAMPARANY Voahangy Chef de l’Unité de Mycobactéries à l’Institut Pasteur de Madagascar Vous avez bien voulu nous aider dans l’élaboration de ce travail malgré vos lourdes préoccupations. Ce travail que vous nous avez confié est aussi le fruit de votre immense expérience. Nous vous exprimons notre profonde reconnaissance. A NOTRE MAITRE ET DOYEN DE LA FACULTE DE MEDECINE D’ANTANANARIVO Monsieur le Professeur RAPELANORO RABENJA Fahafahantsoa Veuillez recevoir l’expression de notre haute considération. A MES ENCADREURS Monsieur le Docteur Jean-Marc REYNES Monsieur le Docteur Jean-Michel HERAUD Sincères remerciements. A TOUS NOS MAITRES ET PROFESSEURS DE LA FACULTE DE MEDECINE D’ANTANANARIVO - DEPARTEMENT D’ENSEIGNEMENT DES SCIENCES ET DE MEDECINE VETERINAIRES. Notre reconnaissance pour tous les enseignements que vous nous avez prodigués. A TOUT LE PERSONNEL ADMINISTRATIF ET TECHNIQUE DE LA FACULTE DE MEDECINE D’ANTANANARIVO. Merci infiniment. papers.title: The necessity of adding Hantavirus infection to the differential diagnosis of Iran syndromic surveillance
papers.abstract: Iran's syndromic surveillance system is continuously monitoring emerging infectious diseases.Given the serological and molecular evidence of hantavirus circulation in rodent reservoirs and the human population of the country, strengthening diagnostic approaches in this system is important.In addition to presenting with manifestations such as renal and respiratory syndromes, hantavirus requires a distinct place in the differential diagnosis protocols of acute respiratory and influenza-like infections.Utilizing existing laboratory capacities, along with ongoing training for early identification of suspicious cases, can significantly strengthen the current surveillance system in managing possible outbreaks and responding to these potential threats
papers.journal: Journal of Health Research and Development

ی در کشت ی کروز در ارد ی بهشت 1405 از مبدأ آرژانت نی به اق انوس ی اطلس جنوب ی بود که توسّط سازمان بهداشت جهان ی (WHO) گزارش و پاسخ بهداشت ی من اسب با مشارکت کشورها ی مربوط داده شد. ا نی ی مار یب به طور عمده به دو شکل تب خونر یزی دهنده با سندرم کل یوی (HFRS) و سندرم قلب ی یویر (HCPS) ده ید یم شود(2). اول ین مورد هانتاو روس ی در ا ران ی سال1982 مشاهده شده و تاکنون شواهد سرم ی و مولکول ی حضور سو ی ها هی مختلف در ج تی مع انسان ی و جوندگان از10 استان ا ران ی(3 .) گزارش شده است کی متاآنال یز نشان داده است که ش وع ی ی سرم ی جهان نیا عفونت و روس ی ی در جمع تی انسان ی 93 /2درصد (است4 ). هر چند با توجه به و ی ها ی ژگ ی ی دم ی اپ ولوژ کی هانتاو روس ی،ها احتمال مشاهده ی ی مار یب به عنوان پاندم ی بعد ی ،کم است ان ی طغ ی ها ّی محل به خصوص در مناطق ی که م زبان ی مخزن وجود دارد، محتمل است. م زان ی کشندگ ی مورد بر اساس هی سو ی ها مختلف از1درصد تا5/ 44درصد (متفاوت است5 .) روس یو آندس (Andes) به دل لی تی قابل انتقال انسان به انسانّ اهمّتی ی اد یز دارد. نظام مراقبت سندرم یک 1 برخالف نظام مراقبت را ی،ج تا زمان تشخ صی قطع ی ی مار یب صبر نکرده و با نگاه به سندرم ی ها ینی بال ی سع دارد طغ ان ی ها ی مار یب شی را پ از تشخ صی قطع ی، شناسا یی و مد یریت کند. عفونت هانتاو روس ی نی از ا هی قض مستثن ی نبوده و با توجه به شواهد ی سرم و مولکول ی مشاهده شده در ا ی،ران الزم است عالوه بر سندرم تب و خون یزیر (6)، در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی سندرم ی ها ( تب و راش حاد7 ( )، شبه آنفلوآنزا8 ) و عفونت دی شد تنفّس ی (9) قرار گ رد ی. در حال حاضر، در کتاب راهنما ی نظام مراقبت سندرم ی،ک عفونت هانتاو روس ی فقط در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی سندرم تب و خون ریزی قرار دارد. قرار گرفتن عفونت هانتاو روس ی در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی ری سا سندرم ی ها فوق م ی تواند به شناسا یی زودهنگام ان ی طغ ی ها نیا عفونت کمک کند . البته در مورد سندرم تب و راش حاد، ا نی سندرم صرفا ً در سو یهی Puumala ده ید شده(است7) که به نظر نم ی رسد سوش را یجی ران ی در ا باشد؛ هرچند مورد آن در ا ران ی گزارش شده(است10 ). در موارد ان ی طغ با سندرم ی ها اشاره شده، الزم است در فرا ند ی بررس ی ان ی طغ (outbreak investigation) یکی از فرض ی ها هی ما ان ی طغ عفونت هانتاو روس ی باشد. در چن نی یطی شرا از ین به بررس ی ها ی مولکول ی و دق تر قی وجود خواهد داشت. با توجه به وجود آزما ی شگاه مرجع تب ی ها خونر یزی دهنده در انست تو ی پاستور ا ی،ران در صورت ارجاع مناسب، موارد جد دی ی مار یب تشخ صی ده دا خواهند شد(شکل1). با توجه به شواهد موجود ی مبن بر گردش هانتاو روس ی در مخازن جانور ی زی و ن ی اب ی رد آن در ج تی مع انسان ی یا،ران توجه نظام مند به ا ین عفونت در چارچوب برنامه ی ها مراقبت ی کشور از اهم تی یا ژه یو برخوردار است. در ا نی ی زم،نه الزم است تأک ید شود که نظام مراقبت یا،ران همانند ی رو کرد اتّخاذشده برا ی یی ها ی مار یب ری نظ تب خون ریزی دهنده ـ مه ی کر کنگو ( CCHF )، از تی ظرف الزم برا ی شناسا یی، گزارش ی ده ی فور موارد مشکوک، حساس ی ساز و آموزش کارکنان نظام بهداشت ی و درمان ی برخوردار است و توان یم نی از ا یز رساخت ها ی برا تی تقو توجه به هانتاو روس ی زین بهره گرفت. ازا نی،رو گنجاندن فعاالنه عفونت هانتاو روس ی در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی سندرم ی ها مرتبط و بازنگر ی ای تکم لی راهنماها ی ی مل مراقبت ب ها ی مار ی و پروتکل ی ها بررس ی ان ی طغ ی ها ینی بال، با اتکا به روش ی ها تشخ یصی مولکول ی، می تواند به شناسا یی به موقع موارد و پاسخ تر عی سر به ا نی تهد دی بالقوه کمک کند. بد یهی است تحقق مؤثر ا نی امر مستلزم آن است که فرا ند ی بازنگر ی و طرّاح ی اجزا ی مرتبط نظام مراقبت سندرم ی،ک با مشارکت صاحب نظران و بهره یریگ از ظرف ی ها تی موجود نظام سالمت .کشور انجام شود 1 (syndromic surveillance) ضرورت اضافه شدن عفونت هانتاو Given the serological and molecular evidence of hantavirus circulation in rodent reservoirs and the human population of the country, strengthening diagnostic approaches in this system is important. In addition to presenting with manifestations such as renal and respiratory syndromes, hantavirus requires a distinct place in the differential diagnosis protocols of acute respiratory and influenza-like infections. Utilizing existing laboratory capacities, along with ongoing training for early identification of suspicious cases, can significantly strengthen the current surveillance system in managing possible طور عمده به دو شکل تب خونر یزی دهنده با سندرم کل یوی (HFRS) و سندرم قلب ی یویر (HCPS) ده ید یم شود(2). اول ین مورد هانتاو روس ی در ا ران ی سال1982 مشاهده شده و تاکنون شواهد سرم ی و مولکول ی حضور سو ی ها هی مختلف در ج تی مع انسان ی و جوندگان از10 استان ا ران ی(3 .) گزارش شده است کی متاآنال یز نشان داده است که ش وع ی ی سرم ی جهان نیا عفونت و روس ی ی در جمع تی انسان ی 93 /2درصد (است4 ). هر چند با توجه به و ی ها ی ژگ ی ی دم ی اپ ولوژ کی هانتاو روس ی،ها احتمال مشاهده ی ی مار یب به عنوان پاندم ی بعد ی ،کم است ان ی طغ ی ها ّی محل به خصوص در مناطق ی که م زبان ی مخزن وجود دارد، محتمل است. م زان ی کشندگ ی مورد بر اساس هی سو ی ها مختلف از1درصد تا5/ 44درصد (متفاوت است5 .) روس یو آندس (Andes) به دل لی تی قابل انتقال انسان به انسانّ اهمّتی ی اد یز دارد. نظام مراقبت سندرم یک 1 برخالف نظام مراقبت را ی،ج تا زمان تشخ صی قطع ی ی مار یب صبر نکرده و با نگاه به سندرم ی ها ینی بال ی سع دارد طغ ان ی ها ی مار یب شی را پ از تشخ صی قطع ی، شناسا یی و مد یریت کند. عفونت هانتاو روس ی نی از ا هی قض مستثن ی نبوده و با توجه به شواهد ی سرم و مولکول ی مشاهده شده در ا ی،ران الزم است عالوه بر سندرم تب و خون یزیر (6)، در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی سندرم ی ها ( تب و راش حاد7 ( )، شبه آنفلوآنزا8 ) و عفونت دی شد تنفّس ی (9) قرار گ رد ی. در حال حاضر، در کتاب راهنما ی نظام مراقبت سندرم ی،ک عفونت هانتاو روس ی فقط در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی سندرم تب و خون ریزی قرار دارد. قرار گرفتن عفونت هانتاو روس ی در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی ری سا سندرم ی ها فوق م ی تواند به شناسا یی زودهنگام ان ی طغ ی ها نیا عفونت کمک کند . البته در مورد سندرم تب و راش حاد، ا نی سندرم صرفا ً در سو یهی Puumala ده ید شده(است7) که به نظر نم ی رسد سوش را یجی ران ی در ا باشد؛ هرچند مورد آن در ا ران ی گزارش شده(است10 ). در موارد ان ی طغ با سندرم ی ها اشاره شده، الزم است در فرا ند ی بررس ی ان ی طغ (outbreak investigation) یکی از فرض ی ها هی ما ان ی طغ عفونت هانتاو روس ی باشد. در چن نی یطی شرا از ین به بررس ی ها ی مولکول ی و دق تر قی وجود خواهد داشت. با توجه به وجود آزما ی شگاه مرجع تب ی ها خونر یزی دهنده در انست تو ی پاستور ا ی،ران در صورت ارجاع مناسب، موارد جد دی ی مار یب تشخ صی ده دا خواهند شد(شکل1). با توجه به شواهد موجود ی مبن بر گردش هانتاو روس ی در مخازن جانور ی زی و ن ی اب ی رد آن در ج تی مع انسان ی یا،ران توجه نظام مند به ا ین عفونت در چارچوب برنامه ی ها مراقبت ی کشور از اهم تی یا ژه یو برخوردار است. در ا نی ی زم،نه الزم است تأک ید شود که نظام مراقبت یا،ران همانند ی رو کرد اتّخاذشده برا ی یی ها ی مار یب ری نظ تب خون ریزی دهنده ـ مه ی کر کنگو ( CCHF )، از تی ظرف الزم برا ی شناسا یی، گزارش ی ده ی فور موارد مشکوک، حساس ی ساز و آموزش کارکنان نظام بهداشت ی و درمان ی برخوردار است و توان یم نی از ا یز رساخت ها ی برا تی تقو توجه به هانتاو روس ی زین بهره گرفت. ازا نی،رو گنجاندن فعاالنه عفونت هانتاو روس ی در فهرست تشخ ی ها صی افتراق ی سندرم ی ها مرتبط و بازنگر ی ای تکم لی راهن…

analysis.summary_en: Background: Iran’s syndromic surveillance system continuously monitors emerging infectious diseases and has serological and molecular evidence of hantavirus circulation in rodents and humans, underscoring the need to strengthen diagnostic approaches. Methods: The authors describe the current surveillance framework and laboratory capacities in Iran, noting the absence of hantavirus in the differential diagnosis protocols for acute respiratory and influenza‑like illnesses. Results: They argue that hantavirus, which can present with renal and respiratory syndromes, should be explicitly included in differential diagnosis lists for acute respiratory and influenza‑like infections. Contribution: Adding hantavirus to the surveillance differential could enhance early case identification, improve outbreak response, and leverage existing laboratory and training resources. Limitations: not reported in the supplied evidence

papers.title: Cardiopulmonary Failure in Hantavirus Disease: Mechanisms, Recognition, and ECMO-Based Management.
papers.abstract: Background: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), also designated hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, is caused by New World hantaviruses, principally Sin Nombre virus in North America and Andes virus in South America. The syndrome is characterized by rapidly progressive noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and myocardial depression, with case fatality rates of 25% to 40%. A 2026 outbreak aboard an expedition cruise ship in the South Atlantic, comprising 13 cases and three deaths, confirmed that Andes virus can be transmitted between humans in a confined setting remote from the rodent reservoir. Methods: Virological, pathophysiological, clinical, and therapeutic aspects of HPS were reviewed, with particular emphasis on cardiopulmonary mechanisms. Sources were identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with priority given to original research articles, clinical series, and controlled trials published through 2025. Literature published in English and Spanish was included. Results: Pathogenic hantaviruses enter endothelial cells and platelets via αvβ3 integrins, disrupting the VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling axis and rendering endothelial cells hypersensitive to physiological VEGF concentrations. Expansion of CD8+ T cells and activated macrophages releases TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma, and nitric oxide, amplifying microvascular permeability and contributing to myocardial depression. Autopsy studies demonstrate direct hantaviral myocarditis with viral antigen in cardiac endothelium and interstitial macrophages. Transpulmonary thermodilution confirms simultaneous hypovolemia, reduced global ejection fraction, and elevated extravascular lung water. Because the incubation period is long and the cardiopulmonary phase is substantially immune-mediated, seroconversion precedes rather than follows clinical deterioration, which preserves the diagnostic utility of IgM serology in a disease that can kill within 48 h. VA-ECMO initiated at the first signs of cardiopulmonary decompensation has reported survival rates approaching 80% in selected experienced centers. No antiviral has demonstrated efficacy in controlled trials during the cardiopulmonary phase, and no licensed vaccine exists. Conclusions: HPS produces a mixed shock state through increased microvascular permeability, T cell-mediated immunopathology, and direct myocarditis. Management follows a stepwise algorithm: suspected HPS triggers immediate complete blood count with peripheral blood smear and concurrent hantavirus IgM serology and RT-PCR, followed by ICU admission, conservative fluid resuscitation guided by transpulmonary thermodilution, and early contact with an ECMO-capable center at the first sign of rising lactate, falling cardiac index, refractory shock, arrhythmia, or rapid oxygenation failure.

analysis.background: HPS caused by New World hantaviruses (Sin Nombre in North America, Andes in South America) has a 25‑40% case fatality, prompting review of its cardiopulmonary failure mechanisms and management.
analysis.main_directions: The review covers rapid non‑cardiogenic pulmonary edema, myocardial depression, endothelial infection via αvβ3 integrins, immune‑mediated microvascular permeability, and ECMO as a therapeutic option.
analysis.current_state: Evidence shows endothelial and platelet infection disrupt VEGF signaling, CD8+ T‑cell and macrophage activation increase permeability, and early VA‑ECMO can achieve ~80% survival in experienced centers.
analysis.gaps: No antiviral has demonstrated efficacy in controlled trials and no licensed vaccine exists; ECMO outcomes are limited to specialized centers, and detailed pathophysiology remains incompletely defined.
analysis.future_research: Priorities include randomized antiviral trials, vaccine development, multicenter ECMO outcome studies, and biomarkers to guide early intervention.

analysis.summary_en: Background: HPS caused by New World hantaviruses has high fatality, prompting review of cardiopulmonary failure. Main directions: The review discusses pulmonary edema, myocardial depression, endothelial infection, immune‑mediated permeability, and ECMO. Current state: Endothelial disruption and immune activation drive disease, and early VA‑ECMO yields ~80% survival in expert centers. Gaps: No effective antiviral or vaccine, limited ECMO data, and incomplete mechanistic detail. Future research: Conduct antiviral trials, develop vaccines, evaluate ECMO across centers, and identify early biomarkers.

papers.title: Hantavirus: A focused review for the emergency medicine clinician.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Andes virus (ANDV), a form of hantavirus, is a potentially fatal disease with several cases recently reported aboard an expedition cruise ship in April and May 2026. OBJECTIVE: This focused narrative review provides a focused overview of the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management of hantavirus infection, including ANDV, for the emergency clinician. DISCUSSION: Human infections with hantavirus primarily occur through contact with aerosolized particles of saliva, feces, or urine of infected rodents or through touching contaminated surfaces. A recent outbreak of ANDV has demonstrated human-to-human transmission in the setting of close, prolonged contact. The incubation period ranges between 4 and 42 days. As hantaviruses target the endothelium of capillaries and small vessels, patients may develop hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, predominantly associated with hantaviruses found in Europe and Asia or hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, mainly associated with hantaviruses in the Americas. Both hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus with pulmonary syndrome present initially with a non-specific viral prodrome (e.g., fever, chills, malaise, myalgias). Following this prodrome, patients with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome can demonstrate coagulation abnormalities and change in urine output with renal dysfunction, while hantavirus with pulmonary syndrome presents with cardiopulmonary symptoms with cough, dyspnea, tachycardia, and hypotension that may progress to respiratory failure and cardiogenic shock. Diagnosis incorporates ELISA assay to detect IgG and IgM antibodies. Patients with concern for ANDV should be isolated in a private room (preferably a negative pressure room). Airborne and contact precautions are recommended; strategies similar to those employed for managing patients with viral hemorrhagic fever may be considered. Treatment is primarily supportive, including resuscitation with intravenous fluids and vasopressors, respiratory support (e.g., supplemental oxygen, noninvasive ventilation, endotracheal intubation), antipyretics and analgesics, and hemorrhage control as needed. Mechanical ventilation, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and hemodialysis may be necessary. CONCLUSION: Hantavirus may initially present with a non-specific viral prodrome, but travel and social history should prompt greater diagnostic suspicion. Patients are managed similarly to those with other viral hemorrhagic fevers.

Objective This focused narrative review provides a focused overview of the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management of hantavirus infection, including ANDV, for the emergency clinician. Discussion Human infections with hantavirus primarily occur through contact with aerosolized particles of saliva, feces, or urine of infected rodents or through touching contaminated surfaces. A recent outbreak of ANDV has demonstrated human-to-human transmission in the setting of close, prolonged contact. The incubation period ranges between 4 and 42 days. As hantaviruses target the endothelium of capillaries and small vessels, patients may develop hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, predominantly associated with hantaviruses found in Europe and Asia or hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, mainly associated with hantaviruses in the Americas. Both hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus with pulmonary syndrome present initially with a non-specific viral prodrome (e.g., fever, chills, malaise, myalgias). Following this prodrome, patients with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome can demonstrate coagulation abnormalities and change in urine output with renal dysfunction, while hantavirus with pulmonary syndrome presents with cardiopulmonary symptoms with cough, dyspnea, tachycardia, and hypotension that may progress to respiratory failure and cardiogenic shock. Diagnosis incorporates ELISA assay to detect IgG and IgM antibodies. Patients with concern for ANDV should be isolated in a private room (preferably a negative pressure room). Airborne and contact precautions are recommended; strategies similar to those employed for managing patients with viral hemorrhagic fever may be considered. Treatment is primarily supportive, including resuscitation with intravenous fluids and vasopressors, respiratory support (e.g., supplemental oxygen, noninvasive ventilation, endotracheal intubation), antipyretics and analgesics, and hemorrhage control as needed. Mechanical ventilation, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and hemodialysis may be necessary. Conclusion Hantavirus may initially present with a non-specific viral prodrome, but travel and social history should prompt greater diagnostic suspicion. Patients are managed similarly to those with other viral hemorrhagic fevers.

analysis.background: Recent cases of Andes virus (ANDV) on a cruise ship in 2026 have raised awareness of hantavirus as an emerging emergency concern (A1) and prompted a focused narrative review for clinicians (A2).
analysis.main_directions: The review outlines epidemiology and rodent‑borne plus documented human‑to‑human transmission (A2, A3, A4), clinical syndromes (HFRS and HPS) (A6), diagnostic ELISA testing (A9), isolation precautions (A10), and primarily supportive management (A13).
analysis.current_state: Hantavirus infection occurs via aerosolized rodent excreta, with confirmed human‑to‑human spread in close contact (A3, A4); incubation spans 4–42 days (A5); patients present with a nonspecific prodrome followed by renal or pulmonary syndrome (A6, A7); diagnosis relies on IgM/IgG ELISA (A9); treatment is supportive with fluids, vasopressors, ventilation, ECMO, and dialysis as needed (A13).
analysis.gaps: There are no specific antivirals or vaccines, limited data on the dynamics of human‑to‑human transmission, and a lack of rapid point‑of‑care diagnostics and clear optimal isolation protocols (A4, A13).
analysis.future_research: Research should evaluate antiviral and vaccine candidates, clarify transmission mechanisms, develop rapid diagnostic assays, and assess the effectiveness of isolation and infection‑control measures (A4, A9, A10, A11, A13).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Recent ANDV cases on a cruise ship in 2026 highlighted hantavirus as an emergency concern (A1, A2). Main directions: The review covers epidemiology, rodent and human-to-human transmission, clinical syndromes, ELISA diagnosis, isolation, and supportive care (A2, A3, A4, A6, A9, A10, A13). Current state: Infection spreads via aerosolized rodent excreta, with documented human-to-human spread; incubation 4‑42 days; presents with nonspecific prodrome then renal or pulmonary syndrome; diagnosis by IgM/IgG ELISA; treatment is supportive (A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A9, A13). Gaps: No specific antivirals or vaccines, limited data on transmission dynamics, and lack of rapid diagnostics and clear isolation guidelines (A4, A13). Future research: Trials of antivirals/vaccines, studies of transmission, development of point-of-care tests, and evaluation of isolation protocols (A4, A9, A10, A11, A13).

papers.title: Omics Approaches in Hantavirus Research: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are zoonotic RNA viruses responsible for two severe human diseases: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Worldwide case fatality rates vary from 1% to 40%. Although single-layer genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics studies have advanced our understanding of hantavirus biology, true multi-omics integration remains scarce, leaving systems-level mechanisms of disease severity and host-pathogen interactions unresolved. High-throughput omics technologies have greatly advanced the study of hantavirus-host interactions. This review summarizes genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and AI-enabled approaches in hantavirus research. Genomic studies have clarified viral diversity, evolution, and reassortment, while transcriptomics has identified regulatory networks governing endothelial and innate immune responses. Proteomics has revealed host proteins involved in immune regulation, endothelial dysfunction, and potential therapeutic targeting, whereas metabolomics indicates substantial metabolic reprogramming during infection, although dedicated studies remain limited. AI-based approaches are increasingly applied to outbreak prediction, surveillance, and risk modeling. Drawing on successful multi-omics frameworks developed for other viral infections, we discuss opportunities to improve biomarker discovery, surveillance, therapeutic development, and future precision medicine strategies for hantavirus infections.

papers.title_zh: 关于汉坦病毒研究的组学方法:最新进展、挑战与未来展望。

analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述概述了基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学以及人工智能驱动的方法在 汉坦病毒 研究中的应用 (A5)。

papers.title: Andes virus and sin nombre virus: Similarities and distinctive features.
papers.abstract: The threat of hanta virus infection has come to the forefront in recent weeks, following the outbreak of the Andes virus aboard the Dutch-flagged MV Hondius cruise ship during its spring 2026 voyage. Several passengers and crew members got infected because Andes virus is the sole known hanta virus to trigger human-to-human infection. All exposed passengers have returned to their countries in Asia, the Americas and Europe, and remain in quarantine to this day because of Andes virus extended incubation period (35-45 days). Several infected patients have died due to Andes high mortality (35-50%). Taken together, the unfolding of these alarming facts has ignited fears of a new hanta virus pandemic. Here, we briefly outline certain among the major similarities and distinctive features between Andes virus and Sin Nombre virus, the two principal hanta viruses known today to infect humans. This writing emphasizes how timely and critical it is to develop concerted research and accelerated testing programs for anti-hanta virus vaccines and antivirals.
